evidence.snippet: Atorvastatin is a selective HMG-CoA reductase competitive inhibitor, used for the treatment of hyperlipidaemia.
evidence.explanation: Atorvastatin is a selective competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, decreasing the enzyme's catalytic activity (stated in a rat pharmacokinetic study).

paper.title: Influence of atorvastatin on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of glyburide in normal and diabetic rats.
paper.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences

evidence.snippet: Atorvastatin calcium, a synthetic stereoisomer of a pentasubstituted pyrrole, prevents the conversion of HMG-CoA by competitive and selective inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase.
evidence.explanation: Pharmacology review confirming atorvastatin acts by competitive and selective inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, blocking conversion of its HMG-CoA substrate.

paper.title: Atorvastatin: a hydroxymethylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase inhibitor.
paper.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists

evidence.snippet: Functional assays revealed that atorvastatin-mediated HMG-CoA reductase inhibition, the rate limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, prevents cholesterol buildup and lipid droplet formation in macrophages.
evidence.explanation: HMG-CoA reductase is identified as the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol biosynthesis; its catalytic activity drives (positively regulates) the cholesterol biosynthetic process.

paper.title: An environmentally relevant mixture of organophosphate esters induces cholesterol biosynthesis in THP-1 macrophages.
paper.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology

evidence.snippet: Atorvastatin, a widely used statin, primarily functions by inhibiting 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in the mevalonate pathway, thereby lowering cholesterol.
evidence.explanation: HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme of the mevalonate pathway (cholesterol biosynthesis); inhibiting it lowers cholesterol, confirming the enzyme positively regulates the biosynthetic process.

paper.title: Atorvastatin as a pleiotropic anticancer agent: mechanisms, evidence, and therapeutic repurposing potential.

evidence.snippet: Functional assays revealed that atorvastatin-mediated HMG-CoA reductase inhibition, the rate limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, prevents cholesterol buildup and lipid droplet formation in macrophages.
evidence.explanation: Blocking the cholesterol biosynthetic process (via HMG-CoA reductase inhibition) prevents cholesterol buildup — i.e. the biosynthetic process increases cellular cholesterol abundance.

paper.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology

evidence.snippet: Atorvastatin, a widely used statin, primarily functions by inhibiting 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in the mevalonate pathway, thereby lowering cholesterol.
evidence.explanation: Inhibiting the rate-limiting step of the cholesterol biosynthetic (mevalonate) pathway lowers cholesterol, confirming the pathway's output is cholesterol.

paper.title: Atorvastatin as a pleiotropic anticancer agent: mechanisms, evidence, and therapeutic repurposing potential.

evidence.snippet: Like other statins, atorvastatin reduces low-density-lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and total cholesterol in patients with hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.explanation: Elevated total/LDL cholesterol is the defining feature of hypercholesterolemia; reducing cholesterol in patients with hypercholesterolemia treats the disease, confirming cholesterol contributes to the disease state.
